concepts.title: State & reactivity
concepts.summary: The same information, held in three different reactive APIs.

react.explanation: useState returns a value and its setter. The parent owns the open door, history, movie list and editor state.

vue.explanation: ref holds reactive state. Script code reads and writes .value; Vue templates unwrap it automatically.

angular.explanation: signal holds each value. Read it with parentheses and change it with .set() or .update().

concepts.title: Rendering 24 doors
concepts.summary: One movie array becomes 24 reusable door components.

react.explanation: map() is ordinary JavaScript. It returns a CalendarDoor for each movie; key uses the stable day number.

vue.explanation: v-for repeats the component. :key identifies each day; colon bindings pass data into props.

angular.explanation: @for repeats the component and track movie.day identifies it. Square brackets bind the child inputs.

concepts.title: Conditional rendering
concepts.summary: The movie title enters the rendered card only when that door is open.

react.code: {isOpen && <>DECEMBER {movie.day}✦{movie.title}Enjoy your movie night}
react.explanation: The JSX expression uses JavaScript &&. When isOpen is false, the back-face content is not rendered.

vue.explanation: v-if includes the back-face content only when isOpen is true. The template wrapper adds no extra element.

angular.code: @if (isOpen()) { DECEMBER {{ movie().day }}✦ {{ movie().title }}Enjoy your movie night }
angular.explanation: @if includes the movie content when the isOpen input signal is true. The surrounding back face stays in place.

concepts.title: Click events
concepts.summary: Each door tells its parent which day was clicked.

react.code:
<button className={`door tone-${movie.day % 4}${isOpen ? ' is-open' : ''}${isToday ? ' is-today' : ''}`}
      type="button" disabled={locked} aria-pressed={isOpen}
      aria-label={`December ${movie.day}, ${state}${isOpen ? `: ${movie.title}. Click to close` : ''}`}
      onClick={() => onToggle(movie.day)}>
react.explanation: onClick calls the onToggle callback prop with movie.day. The parent changes the state.

vue.code:
<button class="door" :class="[`tone-${movie.day % 4}`, { 'is-open': isOpen, 'is-today': isToday }]"
    type="button" :disabled="locked" :aria-pressed="isOpen"
    :aria-label="`December ${movie.day}, ${state}${isOpen ? `: ${movie.title}. Click to close` : ''}`"
    @click="emit('toggle', movie.day)">
vue.explanation: @click emits a toggle event containing the day. Calendar forwards this event to App.

angular.explanation: (click) emits the day through a typed output. Calendar forwards it to the application component.

concepts.title: Component structure
concepts.summary: Each app separates the calendar, door, countdown and editor.

react.explanation: A typed function receives a date prop and returns JSX. This entire file is the small Countdown component.

vue.explanation: A Single-File Component contains TypeScript setup and a template. defineProps declares the date input.

angular.explanation: @Component declares a standalone component and its template. The class contains its input and derived value.

concepts.title: Parent → child → parent
concepts.summary: Values go down; a day number comes back up.

react.explanation: Props contain both values and an onToggle function. Calendar passes that same function to each door.

vue.code:
defineProps<{ movies: Movie[]; availableDay: number; today: number | null; openedDays: number[]; openDay: number | null }>();
const emit = defineEmits<{ toggle: [day: number] }>();
</script>

<template>
  <div class="calendar-grid">
    <CalendarDoor v-for="movie in movies" :key="movie.day" :movie="movie"
      :locked="movie.day > availableDay" :opened="openedDays.includes(movie.day)"
      :is-open="openDay === movie.day" :is-today="today === movie.day" @toggle="emit('toggle', $event)"/>
vue.explanation: defineProps types the incoming data; defineEmits types the outgoing toggle event. Calendar explicitly re-emits the child event.

angular.explanation: input.required declares incoming values and output<number> declares the outgoing day. The template forwards child events.

concepts.title: Only one open door
concepts.summary: Store one day number, not an open flag on every movie.

react.explanation: The setter replaces the current day, or clears it when clicked again. openedDays is a separate history array.

vue.explanation: The ref receives one day number or null. Previously opened days are added to a separate array without duplicates.

angular.explanation: The signal update uses the same conditional expression as React. History is updated separately from the visible door.

concepts.title: Editing movie titles
concepts.summary: A local draft protects the saved movie list until Save.

react.code: {draft.map(movie => )}
react.explanation: The controlled input reads movie.title. onChange maps to a new draft array and replaces just the edited movie object.

vue.explanation: v-model updates the title on the reactive draft object. This makes the input binding shorter in this implementation.

angular.explanation: [value] reads the draft title; (input) calls updateTitle using a template reference. This app uses manual bindings, not Angular Forms.

concepts.title: Remembering opened days
concepts.summary: Persist history while leaving the current open door temporary.

react.explanation: useEffect saves history when openedDays or year changes. Its dependency array is explicit.

vue.explanation: watch observes openedDays and also runs immediately. The toggle handler replaces the array, so this watcher does not need deep mode.

angular.explanation: effect reads history and year signals, establishing its dependencies. All three use the same JSON and localStorage format.

concepts.title: Date locking
concepts.summary: This business rule is ordinary TypeScript in all three apps.

react.explanation: December is month 11 in JavaScript. Unlock through today, capped at 24; other months return zero.

vue.explanation: The same rule is copied into Vue. Available-day state is derived from the current or simulated date.

angular.explanation: The exact same calculation appears in Angular. A computed signal exposes the result to the template.

concepts.title: Countdown & derived values
concepts.summary: The calculation is shared; the way it is connected to the UI differs.

react.explanation: React calls daysUntilChristmas during rendering. There is no useMemo for this small calculation.

vue.explanation: computed derives the number of days from the date prop. The template reads days without .value.

angular.explanation: computed derives days from the date input signal. The template reads the result as days().
